gaps: No public source provides absolute order counts for DTLA/Koreatown or for SoMa/Mission/Tenderloin/FiDi; platform year-end reports give metro rankings and relative indices only, so the orders-per-day input to riders = orders/day / orders per rider per day cannot be sourced publicly at neighborhood granularity.

No SF-specific headcount of app-based delivery couriers was found in this pass: the SF LAFCo/UCSC 2020 study is a sample (n=643) and its PDF was unreachable (redirect to wpmucdn returned 404); whether the full report contains a workforce-size estimate must be checked via the UCSC landing page or the ReWork the Bay mirror.

Third-party transaction panels (Bloomberg Second Measure, Earnest, YipitData) publish only national market share; LA and SF metro share-of-spend is paywalled, and Earnest/YipitData metro cuts did not surface in search at all.
Placer.ai public posts cover metro-level office foot traffic only; DTLA and Koreatown neighborhood series need the paid platform or POI-by-POI use of the free lookup tool.

Google Trends DMA comparison (Los Angeles DMA vs San Francisco-Oakland-San Jose DMA for 'doordash' / 'uber eats') was not run within the search budget; in principle a comparable series exists but it is a relative interest index, not order volume, and must be exported manually from trends.google.com.
LA courier sign-up waitlists (DoorDash/Uber Eats onboarding status by market) were not searched; SF OLSE gig-worker data was not searched; Grubhub city-level reports were not searched.

Ghost-kitchen density: only CloudKitchens' self-reported '11 in Los Angeles' was found; Kitchen United and Reef LA footprints (both reportedly restructured) and any DTLA/Koreatown facility count were not established, and the CloudKitchens site blocks automated fetches (HTTP 403).
DoorDash's State of Local Commerce 2025 references a downloadable dataset and a 90+ page PDF that were not opened; LA-specific downtown-lunch and neighborhood indices may exist there.

The 'greater Los Angeles' vs 'San Francisco Bay Area' DoorDash ranking is metro-scale and undated in the snippet; it cannot be narrowed to the DTLA+Koreatown vs SF-core comparison frame without HMP-internal or paid data.
must_ask_hmp: HMP's SF customer base split by primary working zone (SoMa / Mission / Tenderloin / FiDi-South Beach vs elsewhere) and by platform (DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub) - the only reliable SF-side numerator for the benchmark ratio.

Observed orders per rider per day (and hours per day) among HMP's SF battery-rental and vehicle-rental customers, from customer conversations, app screenshots, or telematics - needed to convert any order-volume proxy into rider counts.
Battery-swap and vehicle telematics ride heatmaps showing where SF renters actually deliver, to define the SF core zone consistently with the LA zone.
Any fleet-partner or courier-program data HMP has from DoorDash/Uber Eats (e.g., active-Dasher counts by zone, fleet-partner dashboards) that no public source replicates.

Geographic origin of existing LA-area inquiries and web orders (Shopify shipping/billing zip codes in 900xx, especially 90005-90007, 90010-90021, 90057) as a bottom-up demand signal for the Ceres Ave hub.
Which vehicle classes (e-bike vs e-moped vs e-motorcycle) SF couriers in the core zone rent, to judge whether LA's car-dominated, longer-distance delivery geography changes the addressable share.
surprises: DoorDash's Nov 2025 State of Local Commerce names San Francisco (with Chandler, AZ) as leading the downtown weekday-lunch rebound at more than 6x the national rate - the SF core zone may be growing faster than the CONTEXT's implicit view of SF as a mature baseline, which affects the SF-benchmark ratio.

DoorDash's own city ranking puts 'greater Los Angeles' first and 'the San Francisco Bay Area' third by order volume, but only at metro scale; nothing found supports a DTLA+Koreatown-specific volume claim.
Placer.ai/IREI report LA office visits still down 36.1% vs March 2019 even after a 16.6% year-over-year gain, so DTLA weekday office-lunch demand may be structurally below pre-pandemic assumptions.

The CloudKitchens 'Koreatown' facility is listed at 1842 W Washington Blvd, 90007, which is south of Koreatown proper (Pico-Union / USC-adjacent) - inside the proposed hub's service area, but a warning that operator neighborhood labels are loose.

The widely cited SF LAFCo/UCSC study appears (from snippets) to report earnings and demographics rather than a citywide courier headcount, so the SF-side denominator may not exist in public form and may have to be built from order-volume proxies or HMP internal data.
